symbols.name: K
symbols.def: The finite number of candidate short-term outcomes.

symbols.name: \mathcal J
symbols.def: The catalogue index set \(\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,K\}\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic treatment level.

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: A generic experimental or observational sample label.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The indicator of membership in the experimental sample \(E\) or observational long-term-follow-up sample \(O\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Observed pretreatment covariates.

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: The persistent unobserved confounder in the observational population.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: The realized binary treatment.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: The signed treatment \(T=2A-1\).

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: A generic signal strength for a binary proxy of \(U\).

symbols.name: W_s
symbols.def: A binary proxy whose conditional mass is \(\Pr(W_s=w\mid U=u)=(1+suw)/2\) for \(u,w\in\{-1,1\}\).

symbols.name: Y(a)
symbols.def: The long-term potential outcome under treatment \(a\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The realized long-term outcome, observed only when \(G=O\).

symbols.name: Z(a)
symbols.def: The full vector \(Z(a)=(Z_j(a):j\in\mathcal J)\) of candidate short-term potential outcomes under treatment \(a\), ordered by measurement time.

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: The realized full-catalogue vector \(Z=Z(A)\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The full-catalogue superpopulation law.

symbols.name: c_j
symbols.def: The known per-unit cost of measuring catalogue outcome \(Z_j\).

symbols.name: b_E
symbols.def: The known base cost of one experimental unit before catalogue measurements.

symbols.name: b_O
symbols.def: The known base cost of one observational long-term-follow-up unit, including measurement of \(Y\).

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: The cap on the catalogue-measurement cost incurred for any main-study unit.

symbols.name: \mathcal D
symbols.def: The ex-ante-known finite family of pairs \(d=(M_d,r_d)\), where \(M_d\subseteq\mathcal J\), \(\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j\le\kappa\), and \(r_d:M_d\to\{1,2,3\}\) assigns every measured outcome to one sequential role.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: A generic admissible measured-subset and role-assignment pair.

symbols.name: d'
symbols.def: A second generic admissible measurement design used in pairwise comparisons.

symbols.name: M_d
symbols.def: The catalogue subset measured under design \(d\).

symbols.name: r_d
symbols.def: The sequential-role assignment under design \(d\).

symbols.name: S_{1d}
symbols.def: The role-one potential subvector \(S_{1d}(a)=(Z_j(a):j\in M_d,\ r_d(j)=1)\) and its realized version \(S_{1d}=S_{1d}(A)\).

symbols.name: S_{2d}
symbols.def: The role-two potential subvector \(S_{2d}(a)=(Z_j(a):j\in M_d,\ r_d(j)=2)\) and its realized version \(S_{2d}=S_{2d}(A)\).

symbols.name: S_{3d}
symbols.def: The role-three potential subvector \(S_{3d}(a)=(Z_j(a):j\in M_d,\ r_d(j)=3)\) and its realized version \(S_{3d}=S_{3d}(A)\).

symbols.name: p_{g,a}
symbols.def: The sample-specific probability \(p_{g,a}=P(A=a\mid G=g)\).

symbols.name: h_d
symbols.def: The unique square-integrable solution \(h_d\) of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]\).

symbols.name: q_d
symbols.def: A design-specific square-integrable candidate selection bridge.

symbols.name: T_d
symbols.def: The operator \((T_df)(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X)=\mathbb E_P[f(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]\).

symbols.name: T_d^\star
symbols.def: The adjoint operator \((T_d^\star u)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)=\mathbb E_P[u(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X,G=O]\).

symbols.name: \|\cdot\|_{2,O,h,d}
symbols.def: For an outcome-bridge perturbation \(f\), \(\|f\|_{2,O,h,d}=\{\mathbb E_P[f(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)^2\mid G=O]\}^{1/2}\).

symbols.name: \|\cdot\|_{2,O,q,d}
symbols.def: For a selection-bridge perturbation \(u\), \(\|u\|_{2,O,q,d}=\{\mathbb E_P[u(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X)^2\mid G=O]\}^{1/2}\).

symbols.name: \|\cdot\|_{w,h,d}
symbols.def: The weak outcome-bridge seminorm \(\|f\|_{w,h,d}=\|T_df\|_{2,O,q,d}\), which measures violation of the design-specific observed outcome-bridge equation.

symbols.name: \|\cdot\|_{w,q,d}
symbols.def: The weak selection-bridge seminorm \(\|u\|_{w,q,d}=\|T_d^\star u\|_{2,O,h,d}\), which measures violation of the design-specific observed selection-bridge equation.

symbols.name: \mu_{d,a}
symbols.def: The experimental bridge mean \(\mu_{d,a}=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)\mid A=a,G=E]\).

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: The observational-population long-term average treatment effect \(\tau=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid G=O]\).

symbols.name: \phi_{E,d}
symbols.def: The experimental score \(\phi_{E,d}=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{A=a\}p_{E,a}^{-1}\{h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)-\mu_{d,a}\}\).

symbols.name: \phi_{O,d}
symbols.def: The observational score \(\phi_{O,d}=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{A=a\}p_{O,a}^{-1}q_d(S_{2d},S_{1d},a,X)\{Y-h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)\}\).

symbols.name: V_{E,d}
symbols.def: The variance component \(V_{E,d}=\mathbb E_P[\phi_{E,d}^2\mid G=E]\).

symbols.name: V_{O,d}
symbols.def: The variance component \(V_{O,d}=\mathbb E_P[\phi_{O,d}^2\mid G=O]\).

symbols.name: c_{E,d}
symbols.def: The per-unit cost \(c_{E,d}=b_E+\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j\).

symbols.name: c_{O,d}
symbols.def: The per-unit cost \(c_{O,d}=b_O+\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The total monetary budget of the main study.

symbols.name: n_E
symbols.def: A generic fixed experimental sample size in the anchor reduction.

symbols.name: n_O
symbols.def: A generic fixed observational sample size in the anchor reduction.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The fraction of \(B\) spent on experimental units.

symbols.name: n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)
symbols.def: The feasible count \(n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)=\lfloor\alpha B/c_{E,d}\rfloor\).

symbols.name: n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)
symbols.def: The feasible count \(n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)=\lfloor(1-\alpha)B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)
symbols.def: The floor-count residual \(\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)=B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}-\{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\) whenever both integer counts are positive.

symbols.name: \mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)
symbols.def: The design-value profile \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) for regular \(d\), and \(+\infty\) otherwise.

symbols.name: \alpha_d^*(P)
symbols.def: The optimizer \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\).

symbols.name: \mathcal V_d^*(P)
symbols.def: The profiled value \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\).

symbols.name: D^*(P)
symbols.def: The oracle set \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\), retaining every minimizer under ties.

symbols.name: \gamma(P)
symbols.def: The scalar separation \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) when \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

symbols.name: \Delta_P(d,d')
symbols.def: The pairwise gap \(\Delta_P(d,d')=\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).

symbols.name: R_d(P)
symbols.def: The best observational long-term prediction risk \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\).

symbols.name: n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)
symbols.def: The continuous jointly budget-feasible sample size \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\) for the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped comparator, which charges one experimental and one long-term-follow-up unit with all measurements in \(M_d\) per analysis pair.

symbols.name: \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)
symbols.def: The secondary cost-weighted diagnostic \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\); the subscript records shape only and does not attribute a published workflow.

symbols.name: \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
symbols.def: The minimizer set \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d(P)\), retaining every tie.

symbols.name: \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
symbols.def: The best-tie profiled design-value ratio of the raw population prediction-risk selector.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: The full-catalogue pilot sample size.

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.def: The nominal noncoverage probability for the post-selection Wald interval.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_m
symbols.def: An independent pilot of size \(m\) observing \(G,X,A,Z,Y\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\), with every component of \(Z\) measured.

symbols.name: \widehat V_{E,d}
symbols.def: The cross-fitted pilot second-moment estimator of \(V_{E,d}\).

symbols.name: \widehat V_{O,d}
symbols.def: The cross-fitted pilot second-moment estimator of \(V_{O,d}\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*
symbols.def: The cross-fitted plug-in version of \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)\) obtained by fitting \(h_d,q_d\) and the two score variances on \(\mathcal P_m\), then inserting the known costs.

symbols.name: \widehat d_m
symbols.def: A deterministic-tie-broken selector \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\).

symbols.name: \underline v_m
symbols.def: A deterministic sequence satisfying \(\underline v_m\downarrow0\), used only to keep the pilot allocation in the interior in finite samples.

symbols.name: \widehat\alpha_{d,m}
symbols.def: The pilot-feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\).

symbols.name: \widehat\alpha_m
symbols.def: The implemented main-study share \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\).

symbols.name: N_{E,B}
symbols.def: The pilot-feasible integer count \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_m B/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\).

symbols.name: N_{O,B}
symbols.def: The pilot-feasible integer count \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon_m
symbols.def: The error \(\varepsilon_m=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*-\mathcal V_d^*(P)|\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: A fixed number of main-study cross-fitting folds.

symbols.name: \widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}
symbols.def: The outcome-bridge estimator for design \(d\) trained off main-study fold \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}
symbols.def: The selection-bridge estimator for design \(d\) trained off main-study fold \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\).

symbols.name: \delta_{h,B}
symbols.def: A deterministic uniform weak-seminorm rate for the main-study outcome bridges.

symbols.name: \rho_{h,B}
symbols.def: A deterministic uniform strong-norm rate for the main-study outcome bridges.

symbols.name: \delta_{q,B}
symbols.def: A deterministic uniform weak-seminorm rate for the main-study selection bridges.

symbols.name: \rho_{q,B}
symbols.def: A deterministic uniform strong-norm rate for the main-study selection bridges.

symbols.name: r_{V,m}
symbols.def: A deterministic rate for uniform pilot estimation of the two source-specific gradient variances.

symbols.name: r_{\widetilde V,B}
symbols.def: A deterministic rate for uniform main-study estimation of the two source-specific gradient variances.

symbols.name: \epsilon
symbols.def: The signal strength of the early proxy in the prediction-selected witness design.

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm p}
symbols.def: The witness design using the weak early proxy and the strong late proxy.

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm e}
symbols.def: The witness design using two moderately informative proxies.

symbols.name: \mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}
symbols.def: The quadratic-form comparison handle for the generic raw population prediction-risk rule.

symbols.name: z_{1-\eta/2}
symbols.def: The \(1-\eta/2\) quantile of the standard normal distribution.

symbols.name: \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
symbols.def: The Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang-normalized experimental score \(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d}\).

symbols.name: \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
symbols.def: The Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang-normalized observational score \(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d}\).

symbols.name: V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
symbols.def: The IKM-normalized experimental source moment \(V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]=(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d}\).

symbols.name: V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
symbols.def: The IKM-normalized observational source moment \(V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]=(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
symbols.def: The profiled IKM-normalized value \(\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}})^2\).

symbols.name: D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
symbols.def: The IKM-normalized oracle set \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)\), retaining all ties.

symbols.name: \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
symbols.def: The best-tie ratio of the raw population prediction-risk selector computed with the IKM-normalized profile.

symbols.name: \theta_d(P)
symbols.def: The identified designwise observed-data bridge contrast \(\theta_d(P)=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\). It equals the causal target only under an additional common-identification condition.

symbols.name: \sigma_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^2
symbols.def: The Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang fixed-system local efficiency lower bound for design \(d\) and causal target \(\tau\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The combined fixed-system sample size \(n=n_E+n_O\).

symbols.name: P_n^{\circ}
symbols.def: The artificial law with source masses \(n_E/n\) and \(n_O/n\) and source-conditional distributions inherited from \(P\).

symbols.name: \lambda
symbols.def: The limiting fixed-system ratio \(n_E/n_O\).

symbols.name: L_0
symbols.def: The fixed number of observational-only cross-fitting folds in the published fixed-design comparison.

symbols.name: S_1
symbols.def: The early short-term outcome in the fixed-system IKM comparison.

symbols.name: S_2
symbols.def: The middle short-term outcome in the fixed-system IKM comparison.

symbols.name: S_3
symbols.def: The late short-term outcome in the fixed-system IKM comparison.

symbols.name: h_0
symbols.def: The true outcome bridge in the cited fixed-system theorem.

symbols.name: q_0
symbols.def: The true selection bridge in the cited fixed-system theorem.

symbols.name: \mu_0
symbols.def: The treatment-indexed bridge mean in the cited fixed-system score.

symbols.name: \mathsf T_0
symbols.def: The conditional-expectation operator in the cited fixed-system theorem.

symbols.name: \mathsf T_0^\star
symbols.def: The adjoint of \(\mathsf T_0\) in the cited fixed-system theorem.

symbols.name: \widehat h^{(-\ell)}
symbols.def: The outcome-bridge fit trained outside fixed-system fold \(\ell\).

symbols.name: \widehat q^{(-\ell)}
symbols.def: The selection-bridge fit trained outside fixed-system fold \(\ell\).

symbols.name: \delta_{h,n}
symbols.def: The weak outcome-bridge rate in the cited fixed-design result.

symbols.name: \rho_{h,n}
symbols.def: The strong outcome-bridge rate in the cited fixed-design result.

symbols.name: \delta_{q,n}
symbols.def: The weak selection-bridge rate in the cited fixed-design result.

symbols.name: \rho_{q,n}
symbols.def: The strong selection-bridge rate in the cited fixed-design result.

symbols.name: V_E^{\mathrm{IKM}}
symbols.def: The experimental score second moment printed in IKM Theorem 5 for a fixed short-term system.

symbols.name: V_O^{\mathrm{IKM}}
symbols.def: The observational score second moment printed in IKM Theorem 5 for a fixed short-term system.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DR}}
symbols.def: The doubly robust estimator in Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem 5.

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{E,B}
symbols.def: The main-study experimental indices, of cardinality \(N_{E,B}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{O,B}
symbols.def: The main-study observational indices, of cardinality \(N_{O,B}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}
symbols.def: Observational evaluation fold \(\ell\) in a deterministic balanced partition of \(\mathcal I_{O,B}\).

symbols.name: e_{B,a}
symbols.def: The number of experimental main-study observations assigned treatment \(a\).

symbols.name: o_{B,\ell,a}
symbols.def: The number of observations in observational fold \(\ell\) with treatment \(a\).

symbols.name: \widehat p_{E,a}
symbols.def: The empirical experimental arm proportion \(e_{B,a}/N_{E,B}\), assigned zero if its source count vanishes.

symbols.name: \widehat p_{O,\ell,a}
symbols.def: The empirical arm proportion within observational fold \(\ell\), assigned zero if its fold size vanishes.

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}
symbols.def: The experimental arm mean of the fold-\(\ell\) outcome-bridge fit, with zero-denominator value zero.

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_{B,d}(a)
symbols.def: The average of experimental bridge predictions and observational bridge residual corrections for treatment \(a\), totalized at zero denominators.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_B(d,\alpha)
symbols.def: The cross-fitted contrast \(\widehat\mu_{B,d}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d}(0)\) at design \(d\) and allocation \(\alpha\), under the declared total convention.

symbols.name: \widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}
symbols.def: The exact arm-normalized fold-averaged experimental plug-in score for observation \(i\).

symbols.name: \widehat\phi_{O,d,B,i}
symbols.def: The exact arm-normalized observational plug-in score for observation \(i\), evaluated with its fold-external fits.

symbols.name: \widetilde V_{g,d,B}
symbols.def: The within-source empirical second moment of the exact arm-normalized plug-in score \(\widehat\phi_{g,d,B,i}\), with value zero when its source count or a required arm denominator is zero.

symbols.name: \mathsf D_B
symbols.def: The event that both selected source counts and every experimental arm and observational fold-arm count are positive.

symbols.name: \widehat s_B^2
symbols.def: The total variance estimator \(\mathbf 1\{\mathsf D_B\}B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\), with all zero-denominator fractions assigned zero.

symbols.name: \widehat s_B
symbols.def: The nonnegative square root \((\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\), hence zero outside \(\mathsf D_B\).

symbols.name: \mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}
symbols.def: The event \(\mathsf D_B\cap\{\widehat s_B^2>0\}\) on which the ordinary studentized statistic is evaluated.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_B
symbols.def: On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), the explicit cross-fitted estimator \(\widehat\tau_B(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\); on its complement, zero. It targets \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\) on the full regular class and \(\tau\) under common identification.

symbols.name: I_B
symbols.def: On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), the interval \([\widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_B/\sqrt B,\widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_B/\sqrt B]\); on the complement, \([0,0]\).

symbols.name: s_{0,B}
symbols.def: The nonnegative square root of \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}\) on positive source counts and zero otherwise.

symbols.name: \mathsf T_B
symbols.def: On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), the statistic \(\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}/\widehat s_B\), and zero otherwise.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_\kappa
symbols.def: The cap-feasible primitive cost vectors \((b_E,b_O,c_1,\ldots,c_K)\) inducing every \(c_{E,d}\) and \(c_{O,d}\) through the catalogue subset formulas.

symbols.name: \tau_0
symbols.def: The fixed-system causal target in the cited IKM limit theorem.

symbols.name: \|\cdot\|_2
symbols.def: The \(L_2(P_n^{\circ})\) norm in the cited fixed-design comparison.

symbols.name: e_B
symbols.def: The floor count \(\lfloor\alpha_BB/c_{E,d_B}\rfloor\) on a deterministic design-allocation path.

symbols.name: o_B
symbols.def: The floor count \(\lfloor(1-\alpha_B)B/c_{O,d_B}\rfloor\) on a deterministic design-allocation path.

symbols.name: n_B
symbols.def: The total deterministic-path count \(n_B=e_B+o_B\).

symbols.name: P_{B,d,\alpha}^{\circ}
symbols.def: The artificial law with source masses proportional to \(e_B,o_B\) and source-conditional laws inherited from \(P\) along design \(d\) and share \(\alpha\).

symbols.name: \|\cdot\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
symbols.def: The \(L_2(P_{B,d,\alpha}^{\circ})\) norm used only for functions having declared versions on both sources or for terms explicitly zeroed outside \(G=O\); it is not applied to an observational equivalence class lacking a declared experimental-source version.

symbols.name: \chi
symbols.def: The arbitrary prescribed finite paired-cost ratio of the prediction-selected witness design to the efficient witness design.

symbols.name: y_{\chi}
symbols.def: The late-proxy signal \(y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-3/(10\chi)}\) in the prediction-selected center design.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)
symbols.def: The \(\chi\)-indexed constrained finite-cell family defined in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\), with relative topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector.

symbols.name: \mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: The observable bridge-law class in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observable\text{-}bridge\text{-}law\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}
symbols.def: The stronger causal full-catalogue subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), containing the latent exchangeability, external-validity, sequential-outcome, and completeness restrictions for every design.

symbols.name: \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}
symbols.def: The relatively open finite-cell perturbation region around the binary witness path specified in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}region}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
symbols.def: The relatively open subregion of \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) on which the strict IKM-normalized optimizer ordering is preserved.

symbols.name: P_{\epsilon}
symbols.def: The \(\chi\)-indexed binary finite-support center law specified in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\).

symbols.name: r_{\epsilon}
symbols.def: The regularity and strict-optimizer stability radius furnished by the binary witness lemma at \(P_\epsilon\).

symbols.name: r_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{opt}}
symbols.def: The alias \(r_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{opt}}=r_{\epsilon}\) used by the corrected binary-region definition.

symbols.name: r_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{IKM}}

definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). definitions.name: Unadjusted and treatment-aware population prediction-risk selectors with secondary paired-source diagnostic
definitions.construction:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), compute the unadjusted observational residual prediction risk and the treatment-aware observational residual prediction risk
\[
R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O],
\]
\[
R_d^A(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(A,X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(A,X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O].
\]
The two generic population prediction-risk rules retain every tie:
\[
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d(P),
\qquad
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d^A(P).
\]
Their best-tie arm-normalized source-score ratios are
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
{\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
\qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=
\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
{\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
For comparison only, define the continuous paired-source count and the secondary cost-weighted residual-risk diagnostic
\[
n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=\frac{B}{c_{E,d}+c_{O,d}},
\qquad
\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)
=\frac{R_d(P)}{n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)}
=\frac{(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)}{B}.
\]
This secondary quantity does not define either prediction selector or any of the displayed ratios. The subscript records only the residual-risk-per-budget shape and does not attribute a proxy-selection workflow or guarantee to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm. Neither population rule is attributed here to a named published proxy-selection workflow.

definitions.name: Independent full-catalogue pilot selector
definitions.construction: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.

definitions.name: Selected-design-only Wald estimator and total variance
Binary two-design arbitrary-cost-disadvantage witness family
definitions.construction:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), respectively. For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and the residual prediction variance is
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]
The primary prediction selector compares this unweighted residual risk itself; paired-cost weighting is retained only as a secondary diagnostic.

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).

definitions.name: IKM-normalized profiled value and unadjusted or treatment-aware risk-selector ratios
definitions.construction:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie unadjusted and treatment-aware population prediction-risk ratios are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
\]
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified. Neither prediction ratio is attributed to a named published proxy-selection workflow.

definitions.name: Relatively open IKM-normalized binary joint-prediction-risk region
Bridge-differentiable regular two-source submodel
definitions.construction:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), and write
\[
 H_d=(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X),\qquad L_d=(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X).
\]
A regular two-source parametric submodel \(\{P_t:|t|<t_0\}\) through \(P=P_0\), with source-conditional scores \(\ell_E\) and \(\ell_O\), is called \emph{bridge-differentiable for design \(d\) at \(P\)} when the following conditions hold.  First, the source-conditional laws are dominated on a common support and the path is differentiable in quadratic mean in each source.  Second, for all sufficiently small \(|t|\), \(P_t\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and its design-\(d\) outcome bridge \(h_{d,t}\) is unique.  Third, after identifying the common \(L_2\) coordinate spaces along the dominated path, there is \(\dot h_d\in L_2(H_d\mid G=O)\) such that
\[
 \left\|\frac{h_{d,t}-h_{d,0}}{t}-\dot h_d\right\|_{L_2(P(\cdot\mid G=O))}\longrightarrow0,
\]
and the conditional bridge equation
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_t}\{Y-h_{d,t}(H_d)\mid L_d,G=O\}=0
\]
may be differentiated at \(t=0\) in \(L_2(L_d\mid G=O)\) using the conditional-score rule.  This is a restriction on submodels, not a consequence of pointwise bijectivity of \(T_d\).

definitions.name: Operator comparison handle for raw population prediction risk
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) to compare the source-score quadratic forms underlying \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)\) with the raw residual-risk quadratic form underlying \(R_d(P)\). These source-score forms have a gradient interpretation only along the bridge-differentiable paths declared for design \(d\). The exact target is a lawwise constant bounding the raw-risk selector ratio \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\); the handle does not assert that a generalized eigenvalue is sharp and does not give an unconditional gradient or causal-efficiency interpretation.

definitions.name: Split-sample saturated treatment-aware pilot selector

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), the observed-data bridge contrast \(\theta_d(P):=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\) is identified. Along every bridge-differentiable regular two-source submodel for design \(d\) at \(P\) in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), its pathwise gradient has source components \(\phi_{E,d}\) and \(\phi_{O,d}\). Hence independent source sample sizes \(n_E,n_O\) have source-score variance
\[
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O},
\]
and this is the gradient variance on the declared bridge-differentiable submodel class. Outside that class, \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) remain source-score variances, but pointwise bijectivity alone does not assert pathwise differentiability. No latent causal restriction, completeness condition, or equality with \(\tau\) is used or asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), and abbreviate
\[
 H_d=(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X),\qquad L_d=(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X).
\]
Observed outcome-bridge existence gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\{Y-h_d(H_d)\mid L_d,G=O\}=0. \tag{1}
\]
Equivalently, \(T_dh_d=\mathbb E_P(Y\mid L_d,G=O)\).  Bijectivity of \(T_d\) makes this solution unique.  Thus \(h_d\), the two experimental means \(\mu_{d,a}\), and the contrast \(\theta_d(P)=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\) are identified from the two observed source laws.

Now take a bridge-differentiable regular two-source submodel in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), with source-conditional scores \(\ell_E,\ell_O\) and bridge derivative \(\dot h_d\).  Differentiability in quadratic mean, the declared \(L_2\) bridge differentiability, and the usual product rule give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \dot\mu_{d,a}
 &={\mathbb E}_P\!\left[
   \frac{\mathbf 1\{A=a\}}{p_{E,a}}
   \{h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)-\mu_{d,a}\}\ell_E
   \mathrel{\Big|}G=E\right]\\
 &\quad+{\mathbb E}_P\{\dot h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)\mid A=a,G=E\}. \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
The selection-bridge equation states that \(T_d^\star q_d\) is the conditional density ratio of \((S_{3d},S_{2d},X)\) in source \(E\) relative to source \(O\), within each treatment arm.  Therefore, for every square-integrable \(f(H_d)\), iterated expectation gives
\[
 {\mathbb E}_P\{f(H_d)\mid A=a,G=E\}
 ={\mathbb E}_P\{q_d(L_d)f(H_d)\mid A=a,G=O\}. \tag{3}
\]

The defining submodel condition permits differentiation of (1) in conditional \(L_2\).  The conditional-score centering term is multiplied by the zero conditional residual mean in (1), and hence
\[
 T_d\dot h_d
 ={\mathbb E}_P[\{Y-h_d(H_d)\}\ell_O\mid L_d,G=O]. \tag{4}
\]
Apply (3) with \(f=\dot h_d\), then apply (4) and iterated expectation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 {\mathbb E}_P(\dot h_d\mid A=a,G=E)
 &={\mathbb E}_P(q_d\dot h_d\mid A=a,G=O)\\
 &={\mathbb E}_P[q_d\{Y-h_d(H_d)\}\ell_O\mid A=a,G=O]. \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting (2) at \(a=0\) from (2) at \(a=1\), substituting (5), and using source-arm positivity to express arm-conditional expectations as source-conditional inner products yields
\[
 \dot\theta_d(P)
 ={\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{E,d}\ell_E\mid G=E)
  +{\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{O,d}\ell_O\mid G=O). \tag{6}
\]
The definitions of \(\mu_{d,a}\) imply \({\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{E,d}\mid G=E)=0\), while (1) implies \({\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{O,d}\mid G=O)=0\).  The nondegenerate-component condition makes both components square-integrable.  Thus they are the two source components of a pathwise gradient on the declared submodel class.  For independent source samples of sizes \(n_E,n_O\), the variances of their sample averages add, giving
\[
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}. \tag{7}
\]
This derivation uses the explicit bridge-differentiability restriction at the differentiation step (4); it does not infer local inverse stability from pointwise bijectivity.  The identification part and the definitions of the source-score variances remain meaningful without that path restriction.  No latent causal restriction, completeness condition, or equality with \(\tau\) was used.
statements.justification: The repaired lemma separates law-by-law bridge identification and source-score variances from the pathwise gradient assertion, which is restricted to bridge-differentiable submodels.
statements.gap: Pointwise bridge bijectivity does not provide local inverse continuity or differentiability of the bridge solution.
statements.consumer: Designers may use source-score variances generally and apply the gradient interpretation only after checking the declared path condition.

For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\),
\[
B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)}\right\}
=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P),
\]
where, once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\),
\[
0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le \frac2B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2}{\alpha^2}+
\frac{V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2}{(1-\alpha)^2}\right\}.
\]
Thus the floor-count source-score variance converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum are
\[
\alpha_d^*(P)=\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}}{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}},
\qquad
\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\left(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}\right)^2.
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), this profiles the designwise gradient variance. For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), it profiles the gradient variance of the common causal target only on that declared submodel class. It is a local causal semiparametric efficiency bound only when the designwise gradient is additionally canonical for \(\tau\), in particular under the fixed-system Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang conditions recorded separately.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), and set
\[
 x_E=\frac{\alpha B}{c_{E,d}},\qquad
 x_O=\frac{(1-\alpha)B}{c_{O,d}}.
\]
The asserted lower bound on \(B\) makes \(x_E,x_O\ge2\). For every \(x\ge2\),
\[
 0\le \frac1{\lfloor x\rfloor}-\frac1x
 =\frac{x-\lfloor x\rfloor}{x\lfloor x\rfloor}
 \le\frac2{x^2}, \tag{1}
\]
because \(0\le x-\lfloor x\rfloor<1\) and \(\lfloor x\rfloor\ge x/2\). Applying (1) to the two source counts gives the exact decomposition
\[
 B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)}\right\}
 =\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)
\]
and
\[
 0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)
 \le\frac2B\left\{
 \frac{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2}{\alpha^2}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2}{(1-\alpha)^2}\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
For fixed \(d\) and \(\alpha\), the right-hand side tends to zero. The left-hand side is the budget-scaled source-score variance; by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}designwise\text{-}gradient}\), it is also the budget-scaled gradient variance along every bridge-differentiable submodel.

Put \(a_d=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}\) and \(b_d=c_{O,d}V_{O,d}\). Positive costs and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\) imply \(a_d,b_d>0\). Direct algebra gives
\[
 \frac{a_d}{\alpha}+\frac{b_d}{1-\alpha}
 -(\sqrt{a_d}+\sqrt{b_d})^2
 =\frac{\{(1-\alpha)\sqrt{a_d}-\alpha\sqrt{b_d}\}^2}
 {\alpha(1-\alpha)}\ge0. \tag{3}
\]
Equality holds exactly when
\[
 \alpha=\frac{\sqrt{a_d}}{\sqrt{a_d}+\sqrt{b_d}}
 =\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}}
 {\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}}
 =\alpha_d^*(P).
\]
This proves uniqueness and
\[
 \mathcal V_d^*(P)
 =(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2.
\]
On \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), the observed contrast equals the common causal target, but the gradient interpretation still requires the declared bridge-differentiable submodel restriction. If that gradient is additionally canonical for \(\tau\), its variance is the local semiparametric efficiency lower bound; the separately recorded fixed-system Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang result supplies that interpretation under its own normalization and premises. Thus the calculation itself is a cost profile of source-score variance and does not, by algebra alone, assert a new cross-design canonical-efficiency theorem.
statements.justification: Profiles the exact two-source gradient variance under monetary costs and quantifies integer-count rounding.
statements.gap: The anchor fixes a limiting source ratio rather than optimizing it under design-specific costs.
statements.consumer: A study designer receives an explicit optimal experimental budget share and minimum profiled variance.

statements.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). For the independently funded full-catalogue pilot selector,
\[
0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m,
\qquad
\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}.
\]
Conditional on the maintained full-catalogue pilot variance condition in Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), together with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\) from Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}variance\text{-}rate\text{-}vanishes}\) and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\),
\[
\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\qquad
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\]
and \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\to0\), with the event empty when \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\). With the stipulated zero value when either floor count vanishes,
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})=o_P(1).
\]
The selector consistently chooses the complete optimizer set under these maintained pilot conditions; no causal interpretation is needed for this observable bridge-functional regret statement. The theorem does not derive the maintained variance condition from a primitive bridge learner.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Write
\[
 v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P),\qquad
 \widehat v_d=\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*,
 \qquad v_*=\min_{d\in\mathcal D}v_d,
\]
and choose \(d^*\in D^*(P)\).  By the definition of \(\varepsilon_m\) and the minimizing property of \(\widehat d_m\),
\[
 v_{\widehat d_m}
 \le \widehat v_{\widehat d_m}+\varepsilon_m
 \le \widehat v_{d^*}+\varepsilon_m
 \le v_*+2\varepsilon_m. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(v_*\le v_{\widehat d_m}\),
\[
 0\le v_{\widehat d_m}-v_*\le2\varepsilon_m. \tag{2}
\]
If \(\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\), the definition of \(\gamma(P)\) gives
\[
 \gamma(P)\le v_{\widehat d_m}-v_*\le2\varepsilon_m. \tag{3}
\]
When every design is optimal, the left event is empty; otherwise finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) gives \(\gamma(P)>0\).

Set
\[
 Z_m=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}.
\]
The maintained pilot variance condition and its vanishing-rate companion give \(Z_m=O_P(r_{V,m})=o_P(1)\).  By the pilot construction and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\),
\[
 \widehat v_d=G_d(\widehat V_{E,d},\widehat V_{O,d}),
 \qquad v_d=G_d(V_{E,d},V_{O,d}),
\]
where \(G_d(x,y)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}y})^2\).  Positive population variances, positive costs, and finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) put all population pairs in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)^2\); with probability tending to one, the estimated pairs lie in a slightly larger such compact set.  The finitely many gradients \(\nabla G_d\) are uniformly bounded there.  Thus
\[
 \varepsilon_m=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat v_d-v_d|
 =O_P(r_{V,m})=o_P(1). \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) imply \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\to0\).

The same compact-set argument applied to
\[
 A_d(x,y)=\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}}
 {\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}y}}
\]
shows that the variance truncation is inactive with probability tending to one and
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|
 =O_P(r_{V,m}). \tag{5}
\]
Finally, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}second\text{-}order\text{-}allocation\text{-}loss}\), whose premises are exactly the same maintained pilot variance condition, its vanishing rate, nondegeneracy, and the pilot definition, gives
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})=o_P(1).
\]
The deterministic tie rule was used only to choose an empirical minimizer in (1); the conclusion is therefore membership in the complete optimizer set, not convergence to an arbitrarily selected population minimizer.  Every stochastic conclusion in the proof is conditional on the maintained pilot variance condition; no primitive bridge learner or variance-rate derivation has been supplied.
statements.justification: The deterministic finite-family inequality turns uniform design-value error into a \(2\varepsilon_m\) decision-loss certificate; population variance positivity makes pilot truncation asymptotically inactive and allocation error second order.
statements.gap: Prior fixed-system allocation rules do not select among distinct bridge equations, costs, and role assignments.
statements.consumer: A full-catalogue pilot can choose the questionnaire and roles with an oracle-regret certificate and the realized allocation-loss order \(O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})\).

statements.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and independent and identically distributed within source. Use the selected-design-only estimator, score moments, total event, variance estimator, statistic, and interval of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}selected\text{-}wald\text{-}variance}\). Impose the maintained estimator-level conditions in Assumptions~\(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}bridge\text{-}product\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}postselection\text{-}multiplier\text{-}condition}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}main\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), together with the four declared bridge-rate vanishing conditions and the pilot and main-study variance-rate vanishing conditions. Let \(m\to\infty\), \(B\to\infty\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\). Then
\[
 P(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}})\longrightarrow1,
\]
\[
 s_{0,B}^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
\]
and the selected observable contrast obeys
\[
 \mathsf T_B=
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}}{\widehat s_B}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta.
\]
All listed nuisance-rate, product-rate, multiplier, pilot-variance, and main-study-variance requirements are sufficient conditions of this conditional theorem. They are not conclusions of the observable law class or of the cited fixed-design theory. Primitive selected-path attainability without additional learner structure remains the separate open object \(\mathrm{oeq{:}primitive\text{-}selected\text{-}path\text{-}attainability}\).
statements.justification: Shows that independent pilot selection can be lifted through a uniform deterministic-path arm-normalized expansion with a fully totalized Wald statistic.
statements.gap: Published fixed-system results do not cover simultaneous pilot selection of proxy roles and source allocation.
statements.consumer: An analyst can implement the exact cross-fitted estimator and confidence interval without undefined rare-event denominators.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), if \(\mathcal D=\{d\}\), the main study fixes positive counts \(n_E,n_O\), and \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\), then
\[
 \frac1B\mathcal V_d\!\left(\frac{c_{E,d}n_E}{B};P\right)
 =\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}.
\]
The right-hand side is the fixed-system two-source pathwise-gradient variance for \(\theta_d(P)\). If \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\) and the fixed-system Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang canonical-gradient conditions hold, it is also their causal semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\tau\); absent those additional conditions only the observable bridge-functional identity is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and the singleton design \(d\).  Put
\[
 \alpha=\frac{c_{E,d}n_E}{B}.
\]
Because \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\) and both counts and costs are positive,
\[
 0<\alpha<1,
 \qquad
 1-\alpha=\frac{c_{O,d}n_O}{B}.
\]
Substitution into the design-value profile gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac1B\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)
 &=\frac1B\left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{c_{E,d}n_E/B}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{c_{O,d}n_O/B}\right\}\\
 &=\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}.
\end{aligned}
\]
By Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}designwise\text{-}gradient}\), the last expression is the fixed-system two-source pathwise-gradient variance for \(\theta_d(P)\).  If \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), the causal-identification premise gives \(\theta_d(P)=\tau\).  Under the additional fixed-system canonical-gradient premises, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) identifies the corresponding two-source canonical-gradient variance as the causal semiparametric efficiency lower bound.  Without those causal-identification and canonical-gradient premises, the displayed equality remains only the observable bridge-functional identity.
statements.justification: The proposition is an algebraic reduction of the paper's arm-normalized profile to its fixed-count gradient variance.
statements.gap: That identity is not an assertion that the displayed moments equal the printed IKM Theorem~5 moments.
statements.consumer: Readers can compare the budget profile with a fixed measured system without confusing normalization or causal-identification scope.

statements.statement:
For the generic raw population prediction-risk rule, the following impossibility holds. For every prescribed finite cost-disadvantage factor \(\chi>1\), the generalized unequal-cost binary witness has paired costs \(5\chi\) for \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and \(5\) for \(d_{\mathrm e}\). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the center law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is regular for both designs and both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\). Nevertheless, \(d_{\mathrm p}\) uniquely minimizes raw prediction risk, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) uniquely minimizes both the arm-normalized source-score profile and the IKM-normalized profile. More precisely,
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon),
\]
and the secondary paired-cost diagnostic obeys
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B).
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(1),
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Across the center family, let \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) be any cost-disadvantage factor minimizing the exact ratio for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\). Then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim \frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the least-divergent sharp elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty.
\]
On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
For each prescribed \(\chi>1\), the center cost vector belongs to \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), has paired-cost ratio exactly \(\chi\), and has a relatively open neighborhood in \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) on which \(d_{\mathrm p}\) remains strictly more expensive and uniquely raw-risk-selected for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\), while both the arm-normalized and balanced-center IKM-normalized ratios diverge along the center-law path. Thus standalone selection by raw population prediction risk has no finite uniform source-score guarantee, even when its chosen design bears any prescribed finite cost disadvantage; even the least-divergent cost-disadvantage sequence grows at order \(\epsilon^{-2/3}\), and its ratio retains the leading divergence \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\). The secondary cost-weighted diagnostic selects the same center design, but it is not the headline rule. No raw-risk proxy-selection workflow is attributed to a published paper, and no claim is made about every predictive method. The IKM-normalized profile has its absolute causal-efficiency interpretation only under the separately stated fixed-system premises; the arm-normalized profile is a source-score design value on the full regular class and a gradient design value only on bridge-differentiable submodels.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and write \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}=P_\epsilon\). Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) proves center-law regularity and common identification, the paired costs \(5\chi\) and \(5\), the strict sourcewise cost disadvantage of \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is uniquely selected by raw population prediction risk, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) uniquely minimizes the arm-normalized source-score profile. Multiplying (1) by the paired costs gives
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}<\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B). \tag{2}
\]
The same lemma gives
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(1). \tag{3}
\]

At every center, treatment is balanced in both sources. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) therefore gives
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon}). \tag{4}
\]
It follows that \(d_{\mathrm e}\) also uniquely minimizes the IKM-normalized profile and that the common factor cancels from the ratios. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) supplies
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}), \tag{5}
\]
as well as
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3} \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}+o(\epsilon^{2/3}). \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]

Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}region}\) chooses each ball inside the radius from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\). Hence every member of \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular, both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), and
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}. \tag{8}
\]
Each center belongs to its corresponding ball. Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) in (5), with \(\chi\) fixed, proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty. \tag{9}
\]
Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}region}\) further shrinks the balls inside the normalized-stability radii without removing their centers. The normalized-stability lemma gives regularity, common identification, and the stated optimizer assignments throughout that subregion. Equation (5) then gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty. \tag{10}
\]
Under its separately stated premises, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) supplies the absolute causal-efficiency interpretation of the normalized profile.

It remains to verify the cost-manifold clause. The center primitive cost vector and cap are
\[
 \left(1,2,\frac{5\chi-3}{4},\frac{5\chi-3}{4},\frac12,\frac12\right),
 \qquad \kappa=\frac{5\chi-3}{2}. \tag{11}
\]
All entries are positive, \(b_E<b_O\), the measurement cost of \(d_{\mathrm p}\) equals the cap, and that of \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is one. Hence (11) belongs to \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), and its paired-cost ratio is exactly \(\chi\). At \(\epsilon=0\), the continuous extensions of the raw risks are \(3/(10\chi)\) and \(3/5\), so their gap is strict. The raw-risk gap, the two sourcewise cost gaps, and the cap inequalities are continuous in the relative topology of \(\mathcal C_\kappa\). Therefore a relatively open cost neighborhood, together with all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\), preserves strict cost disadvantage and unique raw-risk selection. The secondary diagnostic gap in (2) is also strict and continuous, so it persists after a further shrinking.

On this neighborhood, \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}\) stays bounded below and both costs of \(d_{\mathrm e}\) stay bounded above. By (3),
\[
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm p}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 \ge c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}\asymp_\chi\epsilon^{-2},
\]
whereas \(\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*\) stays finite and positive. Thus the arm-normalized ratio diverges. The balanced-center factorization in (4) holds for every positive primitive cost vector, so the IKM-normalized ratio diverges as well. Equations (1)--(11) establish every formula, optimizer, neighborhood, and divergence in the theorem.

statements.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=R_d(P),
 \qquad v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the raw-prediction-order relation and its order-restricted design-value constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P=\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)=\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}. \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P). \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie raw prediction-risk rule is
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty. \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise raw-risk-order implications it exists if and only if \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\). Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact lawwise comparison for selection by raw population prediction risk. The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

More specifically, consider any numerical realization of the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) with the following properties. For each \(d\), it supplies a real vector space \(\mathcal H_d\), a cone \(\mathcal X_d(P)\subseteq\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\) containing a transported law-specific direction \(x_d(P)\), a positive prediction quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}\) on that cone, and two nonnegative source-score quadratic forms \(Q_{E,d}\) and \(Q_{O,d}\), with
\[
 p_d=Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\},
 \qquad v_d=F_d\{x_d(P)\}, \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 F_d(x)=\left\{\sqrt{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}\right\}^2. \tag{5}
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), these source scores are gradient components; outside that class, only the source-score interpretation is asserted. Set
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_+(P)=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)}. \tag{6}
\]
The weakest two-sided quadratic-form envelope on the chosen cones is precisely
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty, \tag{7}
\]
and it implies the valid, generally conservative certificate
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\le\frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}. \tag{8}
\]

The sharp constant in (2) or (3) is not, in general, a largest generalized eigenvalue. Indeed,
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}\right\}, \tag{9}
\]
so the profiled numerator is generally not a quadratic form. If \(\mathcal H_d\) is finite dimensional, \(Q_{R,d}\) is positive definite, and \(\mathcal X_d(P)=\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\), a largest generalized eigenvalue at a fixed \(\alpha\) gives only a one-sided full-space envelope. Selection requires both the upper and lower envelopes in (6), and equality in (8) additionally requires saturation by law-realized, raw-risk-ordered directions. Hence equality with a largest generalized eigenvalue can hold only after adding a common-space representation, a normalization of the positive lower envelope, and the required saturation; none follows from observable-law operator bijectivity or from the raw-risk ordering alone.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Positive unit costs, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\), and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) give, for every \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 0<v_d
 =\left\{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}\right\}^{2}
 <\infty.                                                     \tag{10}
\]
This is a source-score statement on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  By the gradient interpretation recorded in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), it is a gradient-variance statement only along the declared bridge-differentiable submodels.

Because \(\mathcal D\) is finite and nonempty, \(\mathcal O_P\) is finite and nonempty; indeed, it contains \((d,d)\) for every \(d\).  By (10), every ratio in (1) is well-defined, positive, and finite.  Thus its maximum exists, is finite, and is at least one.  If the implication on the left of (2) holds, then for every \((d,d')\in\mathcal O_P\), division by \(v_{d'}>0\) yields
\[
 \frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}\le C.
\]
Taking the maximum gives \(C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\le C\).  Conversely, if \(C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\) and \(p_d\le p_{d'}\), then \((d,d')\in\mathcal O_P\), so
\[
 v_d\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)v_{d'}\le Cv_{d'}.
\]
This proves (2), including the sharpness of \(C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\).

Choose
\[
 d_{\mathrm p}^{\star}\in
 \arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d,
 \qquad
 d^{\star}\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}v_d.
\]
Both choices exist because the relevant sets are nonempty subsets of the finite family.  Since \(d_{\mathrm p}^{\star}\) minimizes \(p_d\),
\[
 p_{d_{\mathrm p}^{\star}}\le p_{d^{\star}},
\]
and hence \((d_{\mathrm p}^{\star},d^{\star})\in\mathcal O_P\).  The definitions and (10) give
\[
 1
 \le \frac{v_{d_{\mathrm p}^{\star}}}{v_{d^{\star}}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P).                                   \tag{11}
\]
The middle quantity in (11) is exactly the displayed \(C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\).  Any constant bounding the best-tie rule at this law must be at least this ratio after division by \(v_{d^{\star}}>0\), while this ratio itself gives equality.  It is therefore the least best-tie constant.  Taking suprema over any nonempty \(\mathcal Q\) proves both uniform characterizations: a finite uniform constant exists exactly when the supremum of the corresponding pointwise least constants is finite.  This also proves that the finite preorder maximum in (1), without any additional operator comparison, is the weakest exact lawwise pairwise certificate.  The dependence on \(T_d\) is already carried by the designwise bridges and the resulting values \(v_d\).

Now impose the stated numerical realization of \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\).  Positivity of \(Q_{R,d}\) on \(\mathcal X_d(P)\) makes every quotient in (6) well-defined.  By the definitions of infimum and supremum, (7) is equivalent to the simultaneous inequalities
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)Q_{R,d}(x)
 \le F_d(x)
 \le \Lambda_+(P)Q_{R,d}(x)                                \tag{12}
\]
for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(x\in\mathcal X_d(P)\), with common strictly positive finite endpoints.  Conversely, any common two-sided envelope with constants \(0<L\le U<\infty\) implies \(L\le\Lambda_-(P)\) and \(\Lambda_+(P)\le U\).  Thus no larger common lower constant than \(\Lambda_-(P)\), and no smaller common upper constant than \(\Lambda_+(P)\), can work.  Since every cone is nonempty, its quotient range is nonempty, and hence \(\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)\).  This proves that (7) is precisely the weakest existence condition for the asserted two-sided envelope and that (6) gives its sharp endpoints.

For any \((d,d')\in\mathcal O_P\), apply (12) at the transported law-specific directions in (4).  The raw-risk ordering gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 v_d
 &\le \Lambda_+(P)Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\}
   =\Lambda_+(P)p_d\\
 &\le \Lambda_+(P)p_{d'}
   =\Lambda_+(P)Q_{R,d'}\{x_{d'}(P)\}\\
 &\le \frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}v_{d'}.
\end{aligned}                                                \tag{13}
\]
Maximizing (13) over \(\mathcal O_P\), and then using (11), proves (8).  The exact finite-order argument above did not divide by \(p_d\), so prediction risks may vanish there.  Strict positivity is required only for the conditional quotient representation in (6).

It remains to establish the profiling and generalized-eigenvalue assertions.  Put
\[
 u=c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x),
 \qquad
 w=c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x).
\]
When \(u,w>0\), direct algebra gives
\[
 \frac{u}{\alpha}+\frac{w}{1-\alpha}
 -(\sqrt u+\sqrt w)^2
 =\frac{\{(1-\alpha)\sqrt u-\alpha\sqrt w\}^{2}}
        {\alpha(1-\alpha)}\ge0.                             \tag{14}
\]
Equality holds at \(\alpha=\sqrt u/(\sqrt u+\sqrt w)\).  If exactly one of \(u,w\) is zero, the same infimum is obtained by taking the appropriate endpoint limit; if both are zero, both sides vanish.  Therefore (14) proves (9) for all nonnegative \(u,w\).

The infimum in (9) need not be a quadratic form.  For an explicit witness, take \(\mathcal H_d=\mathbb R^2\), unit costs, and
\[
 Q_{E,d}(x)=x_1^2,
 \qquad
 Q_{O,d}(x)=x_2^2.
\]
Then \(F_d(x)=(|x_1|+|x_2|)^2\).  With \(e_1=(1,0)\) and \(e_2=(0,1)\),
\[
 F_d(e_1+e_2)+F_d(e_1-e_2)=8,
 \qquad
 2F_d(e_1)+2F_d(e_2)=4,
\]
so the parallelogram identity fails and \(F_d\) is not quadratic.  A largest generalized eigenvalue for a fixed \(\alpha\) can therefore control only the upper quotient associated with that fixed-share quadratic form.  The selection comparison in (13) also needs a strictly positive lower envelope.  Equality further requires transported, law-realized directions that attain the relevant upper and lower envelopes while obeying the raw-risk order.  Comparing design-specific spaces by a single eigenvalue additionally requires a common-space representation and a normalization of the lower envelope.  Observable-law operator bijectivity and raw-risk ordering imply none of those extra properties.  This proves all claims.

For a fixed short-term-outcome system and source-conditional law \(P\), let \(n=n_E+n_O\) and define the artificial superpopulation law \(P_n^{\circ}\) by
\[
 P_n^{\circ}(G=E)=\frac{n_E}{n},
 \qquad
 P_n^{\circ}(G=O)=\frac{n_O}{n},
 \qquad
 P_n^{\circ}(\cdot\mid G=g)=P(\cdot\mid G=g).
\]
Every norm in the statement below is \(\|\cdot\|_2=\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_n^{\circ})}\).  Use a fixed number \(L_0\ge2\) of observational-only cross-fitting folds, independent i.i.d. observations within the two mutually independent sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), and \(n_E/n_O\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).  Suppose Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem~4 statements 1 and 2, their square-integrable latent outcome and selection bridge premises, the corresponding observed moment equations, and both parts of their Assumption~8 hold with nuisance limits equal to the true bridges \(h_0\) and \(q_0\).  Thus, for every \(1\le\ell\le L_0\),
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0(\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{h,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{h,n}),
\]
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0^\star(\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{q,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{q,n}),
\]
all four rates tend to zero, and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,n}\rho_{q,n},\rho_{h,n}\delta_{q,n}\}
 =o(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Define the two score moments printed in their Theorem~5, kept distinct from this paper's arm-normalized \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\), by
\[
 V_E^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \left\{\frac{A-P(A=1\mid G=E)}{P(A=1\mid G=E)}
 \bigl(h_0(S_3,S_2,A,X)-\mu_0(A)\bigr)\right\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=E\right]
\]
and
\[
 V_O^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \left\{\frac{A-P(A=1\mid G=O)}{P(A=1\mid G=O)}
 q_0(S_2,S_1,A,X)
 \bigl(Y-h_0(S_3,S_2,A,X)\bigr)\right\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=O\right].
\]
If these two moments are finite and strictly positive, their Theorem~5 states that
\[
 \sqrt n\,(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DR}}-\tau_0)
 \rightsquigarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,
 \frac{1+\lambda}{\lambda}V_E^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 +(1+\lambda)V_O^{\mathrm{IKM}}\right).
\]
This cited statement records the source's printed normalization only.  It neither identifies \(V_g^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) with this paper's \(V_{g,d}\) nor supplies the arm-normalized fixed-path expansion used by the post-selection theorem.

Let \(\mathcal D\) be finite and nonempty. Suppose the costs and population variance components obey
\[
0<\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\min\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}
\le
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
\qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector. For every \(d\) inside the following maximum, assign the entire floor-count expression the value zero whenever either floor count is zero. Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P\!\left(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]
In particular, allocation estimation enters the profiled value only at second order, and the asymptotically inactive truncation contributes no term to the sharp rate.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 Z_m=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}.
\]
By hypothesis, \(Z_m=O_P(r_{V,m})=o_P(1)\).  Finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) and the displayed uniform bounds furnish constants \(0<\nu_-<\nu_+<\infty\) containing every population variance and every cost.  On the event
\[
 \mathcal E_m=\{Z_m<\nu_-/2\}\cap\{\underline v_m<\nu_-/2\}, \tag{1}
\]
whose probability tends to one, every estimated variance is positive and exceeds \(\underline v_m\).  Hence the truncation in \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) is inactive.

For
\[
 A_d(x,y)=\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}}
 {\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}y}},
\]
the gradients are uniformly bounded on a common compact rectangle around all population pairs.  The mean-value theorem and (1) therefore yield
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|
 =O_P(r_{V,m}). \tag{2}
\]
The population optimal shares form a finite subset of \((0,1)\); hence there is \(a_0>0\) such that, with probability tending to one,
\[
 a_0\le\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\le1-a_0
 \qquad(d\in\mathcal D). \tag{3}
\]

For fixed \(d\), set \(a=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}\), \(b=c_{O,d}V_{O,d}\), and \(F_d(u)=a/u+b/(1-u)\).  The budget-profile theorem gives \(u_d^*=\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt a/(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2\).  A direct calculation gives the exact loss identity
\[
 F_d(u)-\mathcal V_d^*(P)
 =\mathcal V_d^*(P)\frac{(u-u_d^*)^2}{u(1-u)}. \tag{4}
\]
Combining (2)--(4), uniformly over the finite design family, gives
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}
 |F_d(\widehat\alpha_{d,m})-\mathcal V_d^*(P)|
 =O_P(r_{V,m}^2). \tag{5}
\]

On the event (3), both continuous source counts are at least a positive constant times \(B\).  For all sufficiently large \(B\), the floor inequality used in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) applies uniformly and gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 0\le{}&B\left\{
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
 \right\}-F_d(\widehat\alpha_{d,m})\\
 &\le\frac{C}{B}
\end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
with one finite constant \(C\) for all \(d\).  Equations (5)--(6) prove the asserted \(O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})\) bound.  The stipulated zero convention matters only off an event whose probability tends to zero, so it does not alter this stochastic order.  Equation (1) also shows that truncation is asymptotically inactive, which proves the final assertion.

For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), under the sampling and maintained estimator-level conditions of Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}postselection\text{-}wald}\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)}{\widehat s_B}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\tau\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta,
\]
with the same total-event zero extension as in that theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\).  By Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}identification\text{-}class}\),
\[
 \theta_d(P)=\tau\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathcal D.
\]
In particular, \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)=\tau\) for every pilot realization.  Therefore the studentized statistic in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}postselection\text{-}wald}\) is exactly
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)}{\widehat s_B}
\]
on \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), with the same zero extension on its complement.  The theorem's normal limit consequently gives the first conclusion.  Likewise, on \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), its coverage event \(\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\) equals \(\{\tau\in I_B\}\); the complement of \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\) has probability tending to zero.  Hence the coverage conclusion of that theorem gives
\[
 P\{\tau\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta.
\]
