Fix any prescribed \(\chi>1\) and use Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\), the unique raw population prediction-risk optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the unique arm-normalized design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\). More precisely,
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
The paired costs and the secondary cost-weighted prediction objectives satisfy
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi,
 \qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=5,
\]
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +\frac{896}{75(10\chi-3)},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\frac{3872}{25},
\]
and, as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) with \(\chi\) fixed,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
For each fixed pair \((\chi,\epsilon)\), there is a radius \(r_\epsilon>0\) such that every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon\) is regular, has the same strict raw-risk and arm-normalized optimizer assignments, has both bridge contrasts equal to \(\tau\), and satisfies \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)/2\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\). Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) proves that \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\), and the raw-risk and arm-normalized optimizers are uniquely \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and \(d_{\mathrm e}\), respectively. It also proves the displayed raw-risk chain and
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}(\epsilon^{-2}+14)
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +\frac{896}{75(10\chi-3)}, \tag{1}
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\frac{3872}{25},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}). \tag{2}
\]
The cost identities in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\) give
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi,
 \qquad c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=5. \tag{3}
\]
Multiplying the exact residual risks by these paired costs and using \(y_\chi^2=1-3/(10\chi)\) yields
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B), \tag{4}
\]
because \(1-\epsilon^2<1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2\).

We now prove the neighborhood assertion. The center is in the relative interior of the finite-cell parameterization of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\). Positivity of cells, source and treatment overlap, and nonzero determinants of the finite conditional-expectation matrices are open conditions. Matrix inversion is continuous where the determinant is nonzero, so the two bridges, their contrasts, and their source-score variances are continuous on a sufficiently small ball. The variances remain finite and strictly positive there. The constrained model keeps \(Y(1)=Y(0)=U\), randomized treatment in source \(E\), source-invariant proxy kernels, and conditional proxy independence. Thus its causal restrictions persist, and the bridge argument using completeness gives both bridge contrasts equal to the common \(\tau=0\) throughout the ball.

The two raw risks are continuous finite-cell conditional-variance functionals. The profiled values are continuous compositions of the positive costs and source-score variances. Since both optimizer gaps at \(P_\epsilon\) are strict, a sufficiently small radius preserves the two unique optimizer assignments. Finally, the denominator defining \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}\) stays positive and both numerator and denominator are continuous. Because \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)>0\), shrinking the radius once more ensures
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
Taking the minimum of these finitely many positive radii gives the asserted \(r_\epsilon\).

statements.statement:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), and write \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}=P_\epsilon\) for the binary center in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\), with the dependence on \(\chi\) made explicit. Then \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), both designwise bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\), and
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}).
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\) and \(D^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\). The raw-risk-selected design is costlier in each source:
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =\frac{5(\chi-1)}2>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{40\chi}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right),
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\frac{3872}{25},
\]
and the exact center ratio is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac{25}{3872}
 \left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{20\chi(5\chi-1)}{10\chi-3}}
 +\sqrt{\frac{32(5\chi+1)}{75(10\chi-3)}
 \left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right)}
 \right\}^{2}.                                             \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 \ge
 \frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}
 \left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right)
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726},                            \tag{2}
\]
with the identical inequalities for \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\), and
\[
 \inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726}.                            \tag{3}
\]
For all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), the infimum in (3) is attained. If \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) is any minimizer and
\[
 k_\star=\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15},
\]
then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim k_\star\epsilon^{-2/3}.                              \tag{4}
\]
Equivalently, on writing \(\chi=k\epsilon^{-2/3}\), the coefficient of \(\epsilon^{2/3}\) inside the braces-squared expression before multiplication by \(25/3872\) is
\[
 q(k)=2\sqrt{\frac{32k}{15}}+\frac{8}{75k},                \tag{5}
\]
and \(q\) has the unique minimizer \(k_\star\). The sharp second-order uniform elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).                                      \tag{6}
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, the first-order limit in (6) is \(1/726\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\chi>1\), \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), and write \(x=\epsilon\) and \(y=y_\chi\). The center construction has positive finite cells, consistency by construction, randomized treatment in source \(E\), latent exchangeability and overlap in source \(O\), source-invariant conditional proxy kernels, and conditional independence of the early and late proxies given \(U\). Hence external validity and the sequential-outcome restriction hold. For a binary proxy \(W_s\), the two conditional laws given \(U=1\) and \(U=-1\) differ whenever \(s\ne0\); the associated two-by-two conditional-expectation matrix therefore has nonzero determinant. Since \(x,y,1/2\ne0\) and every arm has positive mass, both completeness conditions and both designwise operator-bijectivity conditions hold. The displayed bridges solve the observed equations, and their finite scores have strictly positive variances. Thus \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).

Because \(Y(1)=Y(0)=U\), \(\tau=0\). Completeness and the sequential restriction give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\{h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)\mid U,A=a,G=O\}=U.
\]
External validity and experimental randomization then imply \(\mu_{d,a}=\mathbb E_P(U)=0\), so both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\).

The residual-risk formula from the binary construction and \(y_\chi^2=1-3/(10\chi)\) give
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}
 {1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}. \tag{1}
\]
The denominator in the last fraction minus its numerator is \(3\epsilon^2/(10\chi)>0\), so the fraction is strictly below one. For \(d_{\mathrm e}\), direct substitution gives
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{(1-1/4)^2}{1-1/16}=\frac35. \tag{2}
\]
Since \(\chi>1\), (1)--(2) prove the displayed strict raw-risk chain and \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\).

For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the outcome bridge is \(h(W_y,a)=W_y/y\). At the balanced experimental center,
\[
 \phi_{E,d}=2T\frac{W_y}{y},
 \qquad V_{E,d}=\frac4{y^2}. \tag{3}
\]
In source \(O\),
\[
 q_d(W_x,a)=\frac{16}{15}\left(1-\frac{TW_x}{4x}\right).
\]
Conditional on \(U\), the residual \(U-W_y/y\) has mean zero and variance \((1-y^2)/y^2\). Also \(\mathbb E_P(TW_x\mid G=O)=x/4\), whence direct expansion gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P(q_d^2\mid G=O)=\frac{16(1+14x^2)}{225x^2},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}=\frac{64(1-y^2)(1+14x^2)}{225x^2y^2}. \tag{4}
\]
For \(d_{\mathrm p}\), (3)--(4) yield
\[
 V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{40\chi}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}(\epsilon^{-2}+14). \tag{5}
\]
For \(d_{\mathrm e}\), they yield \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=16\) and \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=384/25\). Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) therefore gives
\[
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\chi,epsilon})
 =\left(\sqrt{2\cdot16}+\sqrt{3\cdot384/25}\right)^2
 =\frac{3872}{25}. \tag{6}
\]
The cost formulas give the two stated sourcewise gaps. Combining (5)--(6) with the profiled formula gives exactly equation (1) in the statement. At the centers, both treatment probabilities equal \(1/2\), so every IKM-normalized source moment is one quarter of its arm-normalized counterpart. Every profiled value is multiplied by one quarter and the ratio is unchanged.

Dropping the first nonnegative square-root term from the exact ratio gives
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,epsilon})
 \ge \frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}(\epsilon^{-2}+14)
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726}, \tag{7}
\]
because \((5\chi+1)/(10\chi-3)>1/2\). Since \(\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the lower bound exceeds one; hence \(d_{\mathrm e}\) uniquely minimizes both profiles. This proves the ratio identities and inequalities.

For the sharp optimization, set
\[
 A(\chi)=\frac{20\chi(5\chi-1)}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 D(\chi)=\frac{32(5\chi+1)}{75(10\chi-3)},
 \qquad C_0=\frac{25}{3872}.
\]
The exact ratio implies
\[
 \epsilon^2\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,epsilon})
 =C_0\left[\epsilon^2A(\chi)+D(\chi)(1+14\epsilon^2)
 +2\epsilon\sqrt{1+14\epsilon^2}\sqrt{A(\chi)D(\chi)}\right], \tag{8}
\]
where
\[
 A(\chi)=10\chi+1+\frac3{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 D(\chi)=\frac{16}{75}+\frac{16}{15(10\chi-3)}. \tag{9}
\]
The objective is continuous on \((1,\infty)\) and diverges as \(\chi\to\infty\) for fixed \(\epsilon>0\). A candidate \(\chi=k\epsilon^{-2/3}\) has leading limit \(C_0(16/75)=1/726\), whereas every bounded sequence of \(\chi\)'s has a strictly larger leading constant \(C_0D(\chi)\). Hence, for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), the infimum is attained at an interior point and every minimizing sequence diverges.

Writing \(t=\epsilon^{2/3}\) and \(\chi=k/t\), (8)--(9) give, locally uniformly for \(k\in(0,\infty)\),
\[
 \epsilon^2\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{k/t,epsilon})
 =\frac1{726}+C_0t\left\{2\sqrt{\frac{32k}{15}}+\frac8{75k}\right\}+o(t). \tag{10}
\]
The rescaled minimizers stay in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\): as \(k\downarrow0\), the positive excess from \(D(k/t)\), divided by \(t\), diverges like \(8/(75k)\), while as \(k\to\infty\), the cross term divided by \(t\) diverges like \(2\sqrt{32k/15}\). Let
\[
 q(k)=2\sqrt{\frac{32k}{15}}+\frac8{75k}.
\]
Then
\[
 q'(k)=\sqrt{\frac{32}{15}}k^{-1/2}-\frac8{75}k^{-2},
\]
which changes sign once, at \(k_\star=\sqrt[3]{18}/15\). Local uniformity and compactness yield \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\sim k_\star\epsilon^{-2/3}\). Finally,
\[
 C_0q(k_\star)=\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968},
\]
which proves the sharp second-order expansion. The common one-quarter IKM normalization proves the same expansion for \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\).

statements.statement:
Fix any prescribed \(\chi>1\). Under the IKM score and profile normalization, every binary center law satisfies, for \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon).
\]
Consequently \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)\). For each fixed \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), there is \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\) such that every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) is regular, both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
On this neighborhood, the IKM-normalized profile is the profiled local causal semiparametric efficiency bound under the fixed-system conditions in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\).
statements.justification: Balanced treatment multiplies both source moments by one quarter, so profiling multiplies every center design value by one quarter and leaves the exact approximation ratio unchanged.
statements.gap: This transfers the arm-normalized impossibility to the published IKM score normalization without conflating the two normalizations.
statements.consumer: The lemma provides the normalized stability radius and the conditional fixed-system causal-efficiency interpretation used by the main impossibility theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
At every binary center, \(P(A=1\mid G=E)=P(A=1\mid G=O)=1/2\). The definitions of the IKM-normalized scores therefore give, design by design,
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d}.
\]
Taking conditional second moments gives
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d}. \tag{1}
\]
The positive homogeneity of the profiled formula, or direct substitution into Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\), now yields
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\left\{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/4}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/4}\right\}^2
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon). \tag{2}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) shows that \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique arm-normalized minimizer and \(d_{\mathrm p}\) the unique raw-risk minimizer. Equation (2) preserves the first ordering, and its common factor cancels from the best-tie ratio. Hence
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon). \tag{3}
\]

For stability, start with the regularity and common-identification ball furnished by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\). Within this finite-cell ball, source-arm probabilities, bridge coefficients, score second moments, and therefore all IKM-normalized profiled values are continuous functions of the positive cell vector. At the center, the raw-risk gap, the IKM-profile gap, and the positive ratio in (3) are strict. Shrinking the ball preserves regularity, both bridge contrasts equal to \(\tau\), the two unique optimizer assignments, and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
This supplies \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\). Finally, when the fixed-system premises stated in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) hold, that cited result identifies the IKM score as the canonical gradient for \(\tau\). Profiling its two source moments over the budget share therefore gives the asserted local causal semiparametric efficiency bound on this neighborhood.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the exact fixed-catalogue raw-risk-selection identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\). Nevertheless, for every prescribed finite \(\chi>1\), the \(\chi\)-indexed binary region satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\), even though the uniquely raw-risk-selected design has paired cost \(\chi\) times that of the arm-normalized source-score-optimal design at the center laws. Across all center cost-disadvantage factors, every minimizing sequence satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the exact least-divergent envelope obeys
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform raw-risk-to-source-score guarantee; optimizing the witness's cost disadvantage does not remove the leading \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\) divergence.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). The family \(\mathcal D\) is finite and nonempty. Positive unit costs and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\) imply, for every \(d\),
\[
 0<c_{E,d}V_{E,d}<\infty,
 \qquad 0<c_{O,d}V_{O,d}<\infty.
\]
Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) therefore gives
\[
 v_d:=\mathcal V_d^*(P)
 =(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\in(0,\infty). \tag{1}
\]
Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}predictive\text{-}benchmark}\) gives
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}. \tag{2}
\]
Substitution of (1) proves the displayed identity. The numerator minimizes over a nonempty subset of the denominator's index set, so the ratio is at least one; finiteness and positivity give a finite ratio. Dividing the best-tie inequality by the positive denominator in (2) shows that its least constant is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\).

For the pairwise comparison, set
\[
 C_{\mathrm{pair}}(P)
 =\max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)}}
 \frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}. \tag{3}
\]
The index set contains all diagonal pairs and is finite; (1) makes every ratio finite. Any constant valid for all raw-risk-order implications must dominate every ratio in (3), hence their maximum. Conversely, the maximum itself makes all implications valid. This proves exactness of (3).

Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}predictive\text{-}impossibility}\) proves, for every prescribed \(\chi>1\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty, \tag{4}
\]
while the uniquely raw-risk-selected center design has paired cost \(5\chi\) and the source-score-optimal design has paired cost \(5\). Their ratio is \(\chi\). Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) further proves
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3} \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}+o(\epsilon^{2/3}). \tag{6}
\end{aligned}
\]
Equations (1)--(3) establish exact lawwise enumeration. Equations (4)--(6) show that neither finiteness of the catalogue nor optimization of the witness's cost disadvantage gives a uniform raw-risk-to-source-score approximation guarantee.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\). For a binary center design having early and late proxy signals \(x,y\in(0,1)\), its treatment-aware observational prediction risk is
\[
 \mathcal R_A(x,y)=
 \frac{15(1-x^2)(1-y^2)(16-x^2-y^2-14x^2y^2)}
 {\{16(1+xy)^2-(x+y)^2\}\{16(1-xy)^2-(x-y)^2\}}. \tag{1}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\frac{585}{1024},
 \qquad
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 \le R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac{585}{1024}. \tag{2}
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
\]
and, at every center,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}). \tag{3}
\]
Hence the exact ratio, the lower bound \((\epsilon^{-2}+14)/726\), the optimizing scale \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\sim(\sqrt[3]{18}/15)\epsilon^{-2/3}\), and the sharp second-order expansion in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) hold unchanged for both treatment-aware ratios.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(X\) is constant and \(Y=U\) on the center family, \(R_d^A\) is the Bayes mean-square error for predicting \(U\) from \((T,W_x,W_y)\). In the observational source, conditional independence given \(U\) gives, for \(u,t,e,l\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
 L_u(t,e,l):=P(T=t,W_x=e,W_y=l\mid U=u,G=O)
 =\frac18\left(1+\frac{tu}{4}\right)(1+xue)(1+yul). \tag{1}
\]
All eight observable cells have positive mass because \(x,y\in(0,1)\). With the Rademacher prior on \(U\), Bayes' rule gives
\[
 E(U\mid t,e,l,G=O)=\frac{L_1(t,e,l)-L_{-1}(t,e,l)}
 {L_1(t,e,l)+L_{-1}(t,e,l)}.
\]
The contribution of cell \((t,e,l)\) to the Bayes risk is therefore
\[
 \frac{L_1+L_{-1}}2
 \left\{1-\left(\frac{L_1-L_{-1}}{L_1+L_{-1}}\right)^2\right\}
 =\frac{2L_1L_{-1}}{L_1+L_{-1}}. \tag{2}
\]
Summing (2) over the eight triples, pairing opposite sign triples, and placing the resulting four rational terms over their common denominator gives
\[
 \sum_{t,e,l}\frac{2L_1(t,e,l)L_{-1}(t,e,l)}
 {L_1(t,e,l)+L_{-1}(t,e,l)}
 =\frac{15(1-x^2)(1-y^2)(16-x^2-y^2-14x^2y^2)}
 {\{16(1+xy)^2-(x+y)^2\}\{16(1-xy)^2-(x-y)^2\}}. \tag{3}
\]
This proves the first display in the statement. The two denominator factors are positive because the summands in (2) have positive likelihood denominators.

For \(d_{\mathrm e}\), substituting \(x=y=1/2\) into (3) gives
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}^A(P_{\chi,epsilon})
 =\frac{15(3/4)^2(117/8)}{24\cdot9}
 =\frac{585}{1024}. \tag{4}
\]
For any square-integrable response, enlarging the predictor sigma-field cannot increase optimal squared-error risk, because conditional expectation is the orthogonal projection in \(L_2\). Since
\[
 \sigma(X,Z_{M_d})\subseteq\sigma(A,X,Z_{M_d}),
\]
we have \(R_d^A(P)\le R_d(P)\). Applying this to \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and using the strict raw-risk chain in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) proves the second display. In particular, the treatment-aware risk gap is bounded below uniformly in \(\epsilon\) by
\[
 \frac{585}{1024}-\frac3{10}=\frac{1389}{5120}>0. \tag{5}
\]
Thus both prediction selectors have the same unique center optimizer \(d_{\mathrm p}\). Their best-tie numerators are consequently identical for each of the arm-normalized and IKM-normalized profiles, proving the two ratio identities. Every exact ratio and every optimization over \(\chi\) then agrees pointwise with the corresponding quantity in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\), so its lower bound, optimizing scale, and sharp expansion carry over unchanged.

statements.statement:
For each fixed \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the radii \(r_\epsilon\) and \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) in Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) may be jointly decreased, without losing any conclusion of those lemmas, so that every law in the corresponding smaller finite-cell ball also satisfies
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)>\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P_\epsilon),
\]
and, in the IKM-normalized ball,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
Thus the radii used to form \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) can preserve both strict prediction-risk orderings simultaneously with the arm-normalized and IKM-normalized optimizer orderings.
statements.proof_tex:
Inside the relative interior of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\), every conditioning cell of \((A,X,Z_{M_d})\) has positive probability in a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(P_\epsilon\). Since \(Y=U\in\{-1,1\}\), the treatment-aware risk has the finite-cell representation
\[
 R_d^A(P)=E_P(Y^2\mid G=O)
 -\sum_v P\{(A,X,Z_{M_d})=v\mid G=O\}
 \bigl[E_P\{Y\mid (A,X,Z_{M_d})=v,G=O\}\bigr]^2. \tag{1}
\]
Every term in (1) is a continuous rational function of the positive latent-cell vector. Hence \(R_d^A(P)\) is continuous for each of the two designs. The source-score and IKM-normalized profiled values are continuous on the regularity neighborhoods already constructed in the two cited stability lemmas.

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) gives the strict treatment-aware center gap
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}^A(P_\epsilon)-R_{d_{\mathrm p}}^A(P_\epsilon)
 >\frac{1389}{5120}. \tag{2}
\]
It also identifies both treatment-aware center ratios with their positive unadjusted counterparts. By continuity, a sufficiently small ball preserves (2), the unique treatment-aware optimizer, and more than one half of each center ratio. Intersect that ball with the radii already furnished by Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\). The intersection contains a positive-radius ball and preserves every earlier regularity, common-identification, unadjusted-risk, and profile-ordering conclusion. This is exactly the asserted joint decrease of the radii.

statements.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). For either positive design-value profile
\[
 w_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P)
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 w_d=\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
\]
the least constant making every treatment-aware prediction-order implication
\[
 R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)\Longrightarrow w_d\le Cw_{d'}
 \qquad(d,d'\in\mathcal D)
\]
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)}}
 \frac{w_d}{w_{d'}}. \tag{1}
\]
For the arm-normalized profile, the smallest constant for the actual best-tie selector is \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)\); for the IKM-normalized profile it is \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)\). Each is at most (1) for its profile and is finite at a fixed regular law. Consequently, a uniform constant over a nonempty law class exists exactly when the supremum of the corresponding best-tie ratio is finite.

If a numerical realization of \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) represents \(R_d^A(P)\) by a positive quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}^A\{x_d(P)\}\) and represents the arm-normalized value by the profiled source-score form \(F_d\{x_d(P)\}\), then the two-sided envelope
\[
 0<\Lambda_-^A(P):=\min_d\inf_x\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}^A(x)}
 \le
 \max_d\sup_x\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}^A(x)}=:\Lambda_+^A(P)<\infty
\]
implies
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)
 \le\max_{\substack{d,d':\,R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}
 \le\frac{\Lambda_+^A(P)}{\Lambda_-^A(P)}. \tag{2}
\]
As for the unadjusted rule, this envelope is generally conservative and the sharp constant is not generally a largest generalized eigenvalue, because profiling the two source terms produces a nonquadratic numerator and equality additionally requires saturation by law-realized, treatment-aware-risk-ordered directions.

Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  For the arm-normalized profile, positivity and finiteness follow from positive unit costs, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\), and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\).  For the IKM-normalized profile, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}source\text{-}arm\text{-}positivity}\) and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\) give
\[
 0<(1-p_{g,1})^2V_{g,d}<\infty
 \qquad(g\in\{E,O\},\ d\in\mathcal D),
\]
so positive costs again imply \(0<w_d<\infty\) for every \(d\).  Thus the following argument applies to either displayed profile.

Define the finite treatment-aware order relation
\[
 \mathcal O_P^A
 =\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)\}.
\]
It is nonempty because it contains every diagonal pair.  If \(C\) satisfies all treatment-aware order implications, then division by \(w_{d'}>0\) gives
\[
 \frac{w_d}{w_{d'}}\le C
 \qquad\text{for every }(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P^A.
\]
Consequently \(C\) is at least the maximum in (1).  Conversely, that finite maximum dominates every displayed ratio, so it satisfies every implication.  This proves (1) and its sharpness.

Choose a design minimizing \(w_d\) among \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)\) and a design minimizing \(w_d\) over all of \(\mathcal D\).  The first design minimizes \(R_d^A(P)\), so the pair consisting of these two choices belongs to \(\mathcal O_P^A\).  Hence the ratio of their profile values is at most (1).  By Definitions~\(\mathrm{def{:}predictive\text{-}benchmark}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\), that ratio is respectively \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)\) or \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)\).  Division by the strictly positive global minimum also shows that each ratio is the least constant for its actual best-tie selector and belongs to \([1,\infty)\).  Taking suprema over a nonempty law class proves that a finite uniform best-tie constant exists if and only if the supremum of the corresponding pointwise ratio is finite.  This is the treatment-aware analogue of the finite-order argument in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}predictive\text{-}operator\text{-}certificate}\).

Now impose the stated treatment-aware quadratic-form realization, with all infima and suprema taken over the cones supplied by \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\).  The envelope definitions give, for every admissible \(d\) and direction \(x\),
\[
 \Lambda_-^A(P)Q_{R,d}^A(x)
 \le F_d(x)
 \le \Lambda_+^A(P)Q_{R,d}^A(x).                           \tag{10}
\]
For every \((d,d')\in\mathcal O_P^A\), evaluation at the transported law-specific directions yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal V_d^*(P)
 &=F_d\{x_d(P)\}\\
 &\le\Lambda_+^A(P)R_d^A(P)
 \le\Lambda_+^A(P)R_{d'}^A(P)\\
 &\le\frac{\Lambda_+^A(P)}{\Lambda_-^A(P)}
 F_{d'}\{x_{d'}(P)\}\\
 &=\frac{\Lambda_+^A(P)}{\Lambda_-^A(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d'}^*(P).
\end{aligned}                                               \tag{11}
\]
Maximizing (11) over \(\mathcal O_P^A\), and using the best-tie bound just proved, gives (2).

Finally, Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}predictive\text{-}operator\text{-}certificate}\) proves the profile identity
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}
 \left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}
 \right\}
\]
and gives an explicit two-dimensional example in which \(F_d\) violates the parallelogram identity.  Thus the profiled numerator is not generally quadratic.  A largest generalized eigenvalue at a fixed allocation supplies at most a one-sided full-space upper envelope; it does not provide the positive lower envelope in (10).  Even when both envelopes exist, equality in (11) additionally requires law-realized treatment-aware-risk-ordered directions to attain the relevant extrema.  Therefore the envelope is generally conservative and the sharp treatment-aware selection constant is not generally a largest generalized eigenvalue.

Choose the radii defining \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) after the joint shrinking in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}joint\text{-}predictive\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\). Then every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular, identifies the common contrast \(\tau\), and satisfies
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\},
\]
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\infty. \tag{1}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) additionally satisfies \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty. \tag{2}
\]
At every center, all four ratios agree. Writing \(P\) for the center indexed by \((\chi,\epsilon)\), for each fixed \(\chi>1\) their common ratio has the expansion
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}),
 \qquad
 \frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}
 =\frac1{726}+\frac5{726(10\chi-3)} >\frac1{726}, \tag{3}
\]
and the same equality holds for each of the other three ratios. Thus \(1/726\) is not the fixed-\(\chi\) leading coefficient. Rather, after optimizing the exact common ratio over \(\chi>1\), any minimizing value of \(\chi\) satisfies
\[
 \chi\sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3}, \tag{4}
\]
and the optimized envelope obeys
\[
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}). \tag{5}
\]
The same optimized-envelope display holds for each of the other three center ratios. The paired-cost disadvantage at the center is the prescribed finite factor \(\chi\). For each fixed \(\chi>1\), the primitive cost vector has a relatively open cost-manifold neighborhood on which \(d_{\mathrm p}\) remains strictly costlier and is uniquely selected by both population prediction rules for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\), while the arm-normalized and balanced-center IKM-normalized ratios diverge. These are constructive objective-separation and unbounded-approximation-ratio conclusions for the two generic population squared-risk selectors defined in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}predictive\text{-}benchmark}\). They neither refute a named published proxy-selection workflow nor cover arbitrary predictive procedures.

statements.proof_tex:
Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\) imply that every arm-normalized profiled value is finite and strictly positive. Source-arm positivity gives \(0<1-p_{g,1}<1\), so every IKM-normalized source component and profiled value is likewise finite and strictly positive. Since \(\mathcal D\) is finite and nonempty, both treatment-aware selector sets are nonempty. Substituting the profiled arm-normalized formula into the definition of \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)\) proves (1), and the IKM definition gives (2). In each case, the selected index set is a subset of \(\mathcal D\), so the ratio lies in \([1,\infty)\), and division by the positive global minimum proves that it is the smallest best-tie constant.

For either positive profile \(w_d\), let
\[
 C_A(P)=\max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,R_d^A(P)\le R_{d'}^A(P)}}\frac{w_d}{w_{d'}}. \tag{1}
\]
The index set is finite and contains every diagonal pair. Any valid pairwise constant must dominate every ratio indexed by this set, while \(C_A(P)\) plainly makes every implication valid. This proves exactness of the third display.

Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}two\text{-}rule\text{-}predictive\text{-}impossibility}\) proves the two-rule regional divergences and the equality of all four ratios at every center. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) supplies the expansion for the two original ratios, and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) identifies the other two with them pointwise. Hence
\[
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho(P_{\chi,epsilon})
 =\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}+o(\epsilon^{2/3})
\]
for every one of the four center ratios. A finite decision set therefore gives only an evaluable lawwise enumeration; it cannot turn either prediction ordering into a uniform efficiency approximation.

Fix \(\chi>1\). Along \(0\le\epsilon\le10^{-3}\), the source probability is \(1/2\), the observational treatment kernel is bounded below by \(3/8\), and every proxy kernel appearing in either design is bounded away from zero by a positive constant depending only on \(\chi\). The two designs have finitely many cells. Hence there is \(c_\chi>0\) such that every observational cell of \((A,X,Z_{M_d})\), for both \(d\), has probability at least \(c_\chi\), uniformly along the triangular sequence.

The training and validation observational counts are both proportional to \(m\) in probability. Binomial concentration followed by a finite union bound therefore shows that every training cell count is proportional to \(m\) with probability tending to one. Since \(|Y|=1\), each saturated training-cell mean satisfies, uniformly over the finitely many cells and designs,
\[
 \widehat f_{d,m}^A(v)-E(Y\mid (A,X,Z_{M_d})=v,G=O)=O_P(m^{-1/2}). \tag{1}
\]
Condition on the training half. The held-out squared losses are independent, bounded by four, and their number is proportional to \(m\). Their empirical mean differs from its conditional expectation by \(O_P(m^{-1/2})\), uniformly over the two designs. If \(f_d^A=E(Y\mid A,X,Z_{M_d},G=O)\), the conditional-expectation projection identity gives
\[
 E\{(Y-\widehat f_{d,m}^A)^2\mid G=O,\mathcal I_{m,O}^{\mathrm{tr}}\}
 -R_d^A(P_{\chi,epsilon_m})
 =E\{(\widehat f_{d,m}^A-f_d^A)^2\mid G=O,\mathcal I_{m,O}^{\mathrm{tr}}\}
 =O_P(m^{-1}). \tag{2}
\]
Combining the held-out fluctuation with (2) and taking the finite maximum proves
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat R_{d,m}^A-R_d^A(P_{\chi,epsilon_m})|
 =O_P(m^{-1/2}). \tag{3}
\]
The zero-denominator conventions are irrelevant with probability tending to one by the cell-count bound.

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) gives uniformly along the triangular sequence
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm e}}^A(P_{\chi,epsilon_m})
 -R_{d_{\mathrm p}}^A(P_{\chi,epsilon_m})
 >\frac{1389}{5120}. \tag{4}
\]
On the event that the maximum error in (3) is less than half the right-hand side of (4), the empirical minimizer is uniquely \(d_{\mathrm p}\). The probability of this event tends to one, proving
\[
 P_{\chi,epsilon_m}\{\widehat d_m^A=d_{\mathrm p}\}\longrightarrow1. \tag{5}
\]

On \(\{\widehat d_m^A=d_{\mathrm p}\}\), each achieved ratio in the theorem equals its corresponding center population ratio. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) identifies these ratios with the original ones, and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) gives
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P_{\chi,epsilon_m})
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{A,\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,epsilon_m})
 >\frac{\epsilon_m^{-2}+14}{726}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{6}
\]
Since the event on which (6) is the achieved ratio has probability tending to one, both achieved ratios diverge in probability. Independence of the pilot and main study, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}independent\text{-}pilot}\), ensures that this pilot selection is a feasible ex ante measurement rule and does not use main-study outcomes. This proves the theorem.

sampling_model.design: A full-catalogue pilot selects \(\widehat d_m\), computes the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\) from pilot estimates of both source-gradient variances and known costs, and fixes the integer counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\); an independent main study then measures the selected short-term outcomes in both samples and \(Y\) only in observational follow-up.
sampling_model.units: Independent superpopulation units from the experimental and observational populations, with implemented counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary complete randomization in the experimental sample and latent-confounded treatment in the observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment overlap within both sources and support overlap across sources are imposed designwise.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The pilot cross-fits both bridges and both score variances for every candidate. The main study refits the selected bridges with fixed-fold cross-fitting. Under the joint main-study law and uniformly over the finite design family and folds, the outcome-bridge weak and strong errors are \(O_P(\delta_{h,B})\) and \(O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), the selection-bridge weak and strong errors are \(O_P(\delta_{q,B})\) and \(O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), all four rates vanish, and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Pilot and main-study source-score second moments are uniformly \(O_P(r_{V,m})\) and \(O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) consistent under their respective laws, with both rates vanishing. The Wald variance uses the realized counts and selected foldwise second moments through \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\).

estimand_functional: The main statistical functional is the selected observed bridge contrast \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\) on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Its explicit selected-design cross-fitted estimator, studentizer, limit law, and Wald interval are given by Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}selected\text{-}wald\text{-}variance}\) and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}postselection\text{-}wald}\), conditional on the declared selected-path learner, multiplier, pilot, and variance conditions. Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}postselection\text{-}wald\text{-}ate\text{-}corollary}\) converts this to inference for \(\tau\) on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\). Absolute fixed-system causal efficiency uses the IKM-normalized moments and the separately cited canonical-gradient conditions.
target_estimand: The causal estimand is \(\tau=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid G=O]\). The observable statistical target selected by the main theorem is \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)=\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\) on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\); it equals \(\tau\) only on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), which contains the binary witness region but not all of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).

tldr: Long-term experiments must choose which short-term outcomes to measure, which sequential proxy role each will play, and how to divide a fixed budget between randomized short-term units and observational long-term follow-up. In the persistent-confounding model of Imbens, Kallus, Mao, and Wang, the proposal makes that design the argument of the local semiparametric efficiency bound. A concrete binary two-design family proves that the uniquely optimal design under the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective, residual prediction variance divided by jointly budget-feasible sample size, can have an unbounded efficiency-loss ratio on a relatively open region even though every candidate remains identified and regular. The equal-cost witness makes the cost-aware ordering reduce exactly to its displayed residual-variance ordering; weakening only the selected design's early proxy then drives the selection bridge and observational gradient variance to infinity. The two source-specific variances also yield a pilot-feasible square-root allocation, integer sample counts, selection control by the oracle separation \(\gamma(P)\), and valid independent-main-sample Wald inference with an explicit selected-score variance estimator under the anchor's weak--strong bridge remainder condition uniformly over the finite design family.

project_justification.gap: The long-term data-combination literature treats the proxy system and sample share as fixed; surrogate-efficiency papers compare availability of a given surrogate vector, while Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm's cost-aware prediction design and other optimal-collection results do not cover persistent-confounding bridge geometry.
project_justification.niche: A finite costed catalogue with sequential role assignments creates nonnested inverse problems whose information contributions differ by source, so residual prediction variance divided by a jointly budget-feasible sample size need not order designs by their bridge-model efficiency values.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs an explicit regular equal-cost binary witness proving that the cost-aware prediction selector has no finite efficiency guarantee, derives the asymptotic budget-normalized design-value profile with an explicit floor-count residual, and implements both proxy-role choice and sample allocation from pilot gradient-variance estimates with oracle-separation selection control and selected-score Wald guarantees under designwise weak--strong bridge rates.

related_work: ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 supplies the persistent-confounding model and observed bridge equations: its Assumption 8 measures each bridge estimator in a weak conditional-moment metric and a strong \(L_2\) metric, its Theorem 4 proves estimator consistency, Theorem 5 gives the fixed-system asymptotic variance under the limiting sample-ratio convention when the better weak--strong cross-product is \(o(n^{-1/2})\), and Theorem 7 establishes the corresponding local semiparametric efficiency lower bound under bridge uniqueness and bijective \(T_d\). The design-value construction is informed by those fixed-system results and uses their weak--strong remainder geometry designwise over a finite family; it does not relabel Theorem 4 as an efficiency theorem. KallusMao2025 characterizes efficiency gains from a fixed surrogate vector when long-term outcomes are limited, but does not choose a costly set or sequential role. CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020, Section 3.2, equations (3.4)--(3.7), shows that in its completely randomized costly-covariate setting the MSE and power design objective is rewritten as residual prediction variance divided by sample size under budget. The comparator here applies that published-workflow-shaped objective to every admissible measurement design by charging \(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d}\) per paired experimental and follow-up observation; the equal-cost binary subclass then makes this cost-aware objective exactly proportional to residual prediction variance. The predictive-impossibility theorem gives a strict non-representability result: this cost-aware criterion has an unbounded prediction-to-efficiency ratio on a relatively open regular region. YangEcklesDhillonAral2024 warns that outcome prediction can differ from causal policy value but does not prove an efficiency-ratio impossibility. LalImbensHull2026 studies regularized combination versus naive screening in a linear latent-surrogate model, not inverse bridge design. TaoZengLin2020 and WangWangMiao2023 optimize phase-two sampling for a fixed measured-variable system. GuptaLiptonChilders2024 learns source allocations in generic moment models but leaves conditional-moment restrictions outside its theory. BennettKallusMaoNeweySyrgkanisUehara2023 supplies stable functional inference for weakly identified conditional moments, while ZhangLiMiaoTchetgenTchetgen2023 treats regular inference with nonunique bridges. MareisDrton2026 derives cost-aware staged measurement for a multivariate linear front-door model, not subset-role selection in the nonparametric long-term fusion model.
technical_internal_limitation: The binary witness establishes pointwise regularity for every positive weak-proxy signal, but its selection-bridge envelope is not uniform as the signal approaches zero; that nonuniform inverse geometry is precisely what generates the unbounded efficiency ratio. Equal costs isolate the inverse-geometry failure from the cost adjustment. The open positive problem is to characterize primitive operator comparability conditions that exclude this path without assuming a design-value bound directly.
honest_scope: The explicit binary family settles the absence of a universal approximation guarantee for residual prediction variance per jointly budget-feasible sample size while preserving identification and regularity design by design. Conditional on the stated finite-family-uniform weak and strong bridge rates, the weak--strong product remainder, and the two variance-estimation rates, the pilot-feasible allocation and post-selection Wald claims are theorem targets. The continuous budget profile is the \(B\to\infty\) limit of the floor-count bound, with the displayed nonnegative \(O(B^{-1})\) rounding residual. Population ties are retained in \(D^*(P)\); \(\gamma(P)\) controls only separation from nonoptimal designs and equals \(+\infty\) when every design is optimal. The sign of \(\Delta_P(d,d')\) is explanatory notation for comparing two profiled values and is not a solve target. A sharp finite guarantee under primitive operator comparability remains open. With a singleton design and fixed sample counts, the formulas reduce to Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem 5's variance and Theorem 7's local efficiency lower bound under their sample-ratio convention.
